section_summary.extract_value: This section describes use of the Body Areas Satisfaction Subscale (BASS) of the MBSRQ (Brazilian Portuguese translation: Laus, 2017) as a 9-item measure with items rated 1–5; an overall mean score was computed and Cronbach's alpha in the present study was .80. The Brazilian Portuguese version has prior evidence of adequate psychometric properties in university women (Laus, 2017). The section does not report sample size, country of data collection, participant demographics, BMI assessment, or correlations with body appreciation.
section_summary.evidence_source: To measure body satisfaction, we used the Body Areas Satisfaction Subscale (BASS) for the Multidimensional Body-Self Relations Questionnaire (MBSRQ; Cash, 2000; Brazilian Portuguese translation: Laus, 2017). This is a 9-item measure that assesses satisfaction with a range of body parts, with items rated on a 5-point scale (1 = strongly disagree, 5 = strongly agree). Scores on the Brazilian Portuguese version of this measure retains all 9 items and has been shown to have adequate psychometric properties in university women (Laus, 2017). An overall body satisfaction score was computed as the mean of all 9 items. Cronbach alpha in the present study was .80.
